vedic_reference.note: Pragnaan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'प्रज्ञान' which means 'wisdom, knowledge'. It is formed from the root 'ज्ञान' meaning 'knowledge'. The long-meaning 'ज्ञानमूलतम प्रज्ञा' means 'the root of wisdom is knowledge'. Pragnaan is a modern and unique name that carries the essence of wisdom and knowledge.

historical_references.reference: Pragnaan was a celebrated sage and scholar during the Gupta period (c. 320 to 550 CE) in ancient India. He is famous for his contributions to Jain philosophy and literature. Pragnaan's works include commentaries on various Jain texts and original works on logic and metaphysics.

Pragnaan is also revered in Hindu tradition as one of the fifty-two Bhagavatas, or divine beings, who were believed to have directly experienced and manifested the divine presence of Lord Vishnu. This reference dates back to medieval India (c. 7th to 13th centuries CE).
